The Theatre Arts and Motion Pictures Practitioners Association of Nigeria has inaugurated its newly elected national executive, with veteran Yoruba actor, Akeem Olayiwola, popularly known as Ajala Jalingo, emerging as its new global president. The inauguration took place on November 25 at the association’s national manifesto, election, awards and swearing-in ceremony. The event also marked the end of Bolaji Amusan’s eight-year tenure as TAMPAN’s global president, as he formally handed over leadership to Olayiwola. In his farewell address, Amusan expressed gratitude for the opportunity to lead the association, describing his tenure as an honour and a fulfilling experience. He also reaffirmed his commitment to TAMPAN, noting that his exit from the presidency would not end his involvement in the association’s affairs. Their inauguration followed an earlier election in which Olayiwola emerged as the association’s global president. An Egba-born filmmaker from Ogun State, Olayiwola has been active in the Yoruba movie industry since the mid-1990s. He previously served in the leadership of the Lagos State chapter of the Association of Nigerian Theatre Arts Practitioners before emerging as TAMPAN’s global president. The new executive is expected to lead the association and advance the interests of practitioners in Nigeria’s theatre and motion picture industry. Kindly share this story:
